LAREDO, Texas — Texas A&M International University is hosting a traveling exhibit and documentary film, “Ancient Landscapes of South Texas: Hiding in Plain Sight,” with a free opening reception and documentary screening set for Tuesday, Oct. 27, at 6 p.m. in Student Center Room 236, according to TAMIU.

Admission is free and open to both the TAMIU community and the public.

The exhibit is on display on the second floor of the Senator Judith Zaffirini Student Success Center through Tuesday, Dec. 15. The center is open Monday and Tuesday from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Wednesday and Thursday from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m., and Friday from 8 a.m. to 3 p.m.

The exhibit and documentary are made possible through the Community Historical Archaeology Project with Schools (CHAPS) program at the University of Texas Rio Grande Valley, in collaboration with TAMIU’s College of Arts and Sciences and Department of Social Sciences.

Together they cover 50 million years of natural history and 15,000 years of cultural history in the Rio Grande Valley — from Pleistocene hunters to Spanish rancheros to the construction of dams and wind turbines. Highlights include volcanic eruptions, 27-million-year-old petrified logs, 43-million-year-old giant oyster shells, and projectile points crafted by humans for more than 15,000 years.

Dr. Alison Hadley, TAMIU associate professor of Anthropology, said the university “continues to create a home for opportunities that connect academic inquiry with the community’s shared history.”

More information is available at www.utrgv.edu/chaps or by emailing chaps@utrgv.edu.
